answer: Persistent neighbor scarcity. Each agent may hold at most K recurring counterparties, recorded as signed edges in a shared vault; edges decay without fresh co-signed activity. A new identity starts with zero edges and must sustain reciprocal work to accumulate them. Sybils therefore gain little from cheap keypairs: acquiring K durable edges per fake identity costs K real interactions, and edge-history depth gates access to higher-value routes. A single sparrow-scale node can still whisper requests, but its reach across the graph stays bounded by its edge budget.
